summary_en: This case checks calculate_heat_flows against equation T2 of design report Section 4.2, the battery example of Section 4.3 and the checks of Section 5.5. The evidence file of precondition PA-001 records a pass with all 114 checks passed, and it was written after the last modification time of the thermal module source files. In this case the five connection thermal resistances are assembled by assemble_thermal_parameters according to equation T5; SR, JC, CR, BR and DR are 0.8, 0.09, 0.12, 0.5 and 1.5 K/W in that order, in agreement with the hand calculation. The battery example takes the battery temperature $T_B$ as 303 K, the radiator temperature $T_R$ as 300 K and $R_BR$ as 0.5 K/W, and the computed $q_BR$ is 6 W. With the two end temperatures swapped it is −6 W, and with both ends at 300 K and both ends at 303 K it is 0 W and 0 W respectively; all three $q_BR$ results agree with the expected values. For each of the five connections, swapping the two end temperatures reverses the sign of the heat flow and keeps its magnitude, and with the two ends of a connection at equal temperature the heat flow of that connection is exactly zero. With all six node temperatures at 293.15 K the heat flows of all five connections are zero. The heat flow is positive when the first node is hotter and negative when it is colder; a positive value means flow from the first node of the path name to the second node. In total 160 heat flow values were compared with the hand calculation or an independent exact calculation; the largest relative error over nonzero reference values is 9.7×10^{−17}, within the acceptance limit of 1×10^{−12}, and all 12 heat flow values with a zero reference are exactly zero. Instrumented counts show that in one call each of the five paths is evaluated once, the thermal resistance of each path is read 1 time, and each node temperature is read as many times as the number of paths connected to that node. The end temperatures are read in the order S, R, J, C, C, R, B, R, D, R, the thermal resistances are read in the order SR, JC, CR, BR, DR, and the next path is read only after both end temperatures and the thermal resistance of the current path have been read. Raising any node temperature by 1 K changes only the heat flows of the paths connected to that node. One evaluation of thermal_derivative calls calculate_heat_flows 1 time and reuses its heat flows. State and parameters are bitwise identical before and after the call, the returned result contains only heat flows and shares no memory with the inputs, and repeated calls give bitwise identical results. Of 36 invalid inputs covering missing nodes, wrong array order, wrong array shape or type, zero or negative thermal resistance, non-finite inputs and unassembled connections, all 36 raise a definite error naming the specific field, and none returns a result. The 6 wrong array order inputs change only the node_order or path_order declared by the parameter object and are all detected from that declaration; state temperatures given with node names as keys are rejected regardless of key order. Under valid extreme inputs the overridden $R_CR$ is 1×10^{−4} K/W and $R_DR$ is 1000001.25 K/W, in agreement with the calculation from the override values and equation T5; $q_CR$ is 1.1×10^{6} W and $q_DR$ is 9.5×10^{−5} W, and with $T_B$ higher than $T_R$ by 2^{−20} K, $q_BR$ is 1.9×10^{−6} W. The largest relative error of the five connection heat flows against equation T2 is 7.3×10^{−17}, and no value is set to zero or truncated.
